attributes.action: Call a COBRA meeting over wildfire risk
attributes.additional_details:
I am calling on the UK government to call a COBRA meeting to discuss all possible measures for management of wildfire risk so we are better prepared for 2027 including: 
1. Ban the sale of disposable BBQs 
2. Ban the sale of fireworks to general public
3. Spot purchase by UK govt of firefighting media including water bombers 
4. Put all resource on the table for recruitment of firefighters on retained duty system
5. Meet stakeholders like gamekeepers and FBU and other SMEs
attributes.background: July 2026 is set to be the hottest in 200 years, and the UK is burning with multiple wildfires in Scotland, Wales and England destroying ecosystems that have been here for decades, risking lives. Its time for action now.

rejection.details:
The Prime Minister chaired a Cobra committee meeting on 12 August on the UK’s ongoing response to extreme heat, wildfires and drought.

The sale of disposable BBQs has been temporarily banned in England, Scotland and Wales: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/statutory-guidelines-on-disposable-bbqs

You may wish to sign this petition, which is already open: "Outlaw fireworks for the general public" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/766448

Responsibility for fire and rescue services is devolved to the Welsh Government and Welsh Parliament. The Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send a petition about fire and rescue services in Wales to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

You may also wish to raise your concerns with your local Members of the Senedd who represent you. You can find out who your Members of the Senedd are and how to contact them here: https://senedd.wales/find-a-member-of-the-senedd/
